records.source: פַּלְגֵי־מַ֣יִם לֶב־מֶ֭לֶךְ בְּיַד־יְהוָ֑ה עַֽל־כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֖ר יַחְפֹּ֣ץ יַטֶּֽנּוּ׃
records.gloss: Channels of water [is the] heart of a king in [the] hand of YHWH; to all that he desires he turns it.
pieces: A king's heart is like streams of water in the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q who directs it wherever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} pleases.

L.1: [Like] channels of water [is the] heart of a king in [the] hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} turns it wherever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} desires.

R.1: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} guides a king's thoughts the way a farmer guides water along a ditch. \q He turns the king's heart wherever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wants.

decisions.choice: channels of water: irrigation channels that are steered where they are needed
decisions.reason: The word (peleg) is a channel or watercourse (5:16; Psalm 1:3). As a farmer cuts the channel to lead the water, the LORD leads even the most powerful human will.

decisions.choice: God's rule over rulers
decisions.reason: Even a king, whose word decides for others (16:10; 20:8), is not outside God's control (16:1, 9; Ezra 7:27).

decisions.choice: the way a farmer guides water along a ditch
decisions.reason: Readable names the farmer to make the irrigation picture plain.

records.source: כָּֽל־דֶּרֶךְ־אִ֭ישׁ יָשָׁ֣ר בְּעֵינָ֑יו וְתֹכֵ֖ן לִבּ֣וֹת יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Every way of a person [is] upright in his eyes, and YHWH weighs hearts.
pieces: People think every road they take is right, \q but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} weighs the heart.

L.2: Every way of a person [is] right in {{gender:their|his}} own eyes, \q but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} weighs [the] hearts.

R.2: People always believe that what they do is right. \q But {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} sees what is really in their hearts.

decisions.choice: weighs hearts: tests motives, as in 16:2
decisions.reason: Nearly the same saying stands in 16:2, with "spirits" for "hearts" and "pure" for "right"; compare 12:15 and 24:12.

records.source: עֲ֭שֹׂה צְדָקָ֣ה וּמִשְׁפָּ֑ט נִבְחָ֖ר לַיהוָ֣ה מִזָּֽבַח׃
records.gloss: To do righteousness and justice [is] chosen by YHWH more than sacrifice.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} would rather see people do what is right and just \q than offer sacrifice.

L.3: To do righteousness and justice \q [is] preferred by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} more than sacrifice.

R.3: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} wants people to do what is right and fair. \q That matters more to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} than offering sacrifices.

decisions.choice: right living over ritual
decisions.reason: The prophets say the same (1 Samuel 15:22; Hosea 6:6; Micah 6:6–8). Sacrifice is not rejected; it is worthless without justice (verse 27; 15:8).

records.source: רוּם־עֵ֭ינַיִם וּרְחַב־לֵ֑ב נִ֖ר רְשָׁעִ֣ים חַטָּֽאת׃
records.gloss: Haughtiness of eyes and wideness of heart, [the] lamp of [the] wicked, [is] sin.
pieces: Proud eyes and an arrogant heart, \q the lamp that lights the way of the wicked, are sin.

L.4: Haughty eyes and a swollen heart, \q [the] lamp of [the] wicked, [are] sin.

R.4: Proud looks and a proud heart are sin. \q Yet that pride is the light wicked people live by.

decisions.choice: haughty eyes and a wide heart: pride and arrogance
decisions.reason: Raised eyes are pride (6:17; 30:13); a wide heart is an inflated, arrogant mind (Psalm 101:5).

decisions.choice: lamp (ner): what guides or marks the wicked
alternatives: the plowed ground of the wicked (nir): what they produce
decisions.reason: The consonants can be read as "lamp" (as the vowels have it, compare 13:9; 20:27) or as "newly plowed ground" (nir, 13:23; Jeremiah 4:3), that is, the crop the wicked produce. Either way, their pride and all it yields is sin.

records.source: מַחְשְׁב֣וֹת חָ֭רוּץ אַךְ־לְמוֹתָ֑ר וְכָל־אָ֝֗ץ אַךְ־לְמַחְסֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: [The] plans of a diligent [person are] only to profit, and every [one who] hastens [is] only to lack.
pieces: The plans of the diligent bring nothing but gain, \q but all who rush in haste come to nothing but need.

L.5: [The] plans of [the] diligent [lead] only to profit, \q but everyone who hurries [comes] only to want.

R.5: Hard workers who plan carefully will have plenty. \q People who rush into things end up poor.

decisions.choice: diligent against hasty: careful effort against rash shortcuts
decisions.reason: The diligent (harus) appear in 10:4 and 13:4. The one who hurries acts without thought or grabs for quick gain (19:2; 28:20). The double "only" (ak) sets the two outcomes side by side.

records.source: פֹּ֣עַל א֭וֹצָרוֹת בִּלְשׁ֣וֹן שָׁ֑קֶר הֶ֥בֶל נִ֝דָּ֗ף מְבַקְשֵׁי־מָֽוֶת׃
records.gloss: [The] acquisition of treasures by a tongue of falsehood [is] a breath driven about, seekers of death.
pieces: Riches gained by a lying tongue are a mist that drifts away, \q and those who seek them seek death.

L.6: Getting treasures by a lying tongue [is] a vapor blown away; \q [they are] seekers of death.

R.6: Money gained by lying vanishes like a breath on the wind. \q People who get rich that way are heading toward death.

decisions.choice: a vapor blown away: gain that vanishes
decisions.reason: Breath (hevel) is what does not last (13:11; Ecclesiastes 1:2); driven about, it is soon gone.

decisions.choice: seekers of death
alternatives: snares of death (Greek and some Hebrew manuscripts)
decisions.reason: The standard Hebrew text reads "seekers of death": those who gain this way are pursuing their own death (8:36). The Greek translation and some Hebrew manuscripts read "snares of death" (with a slightly different word, compare 13:14; 14:27), which makes the riches a deadly trap.

records.source: שֹׁד־רְשָׁעִ֥ים יְגוֹרֵ֑ם כִּ֥י מֵ֝אֲנ֗וּ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת מִשְׁפָּֽט׃
records.gloss: [The] violence of [the] wicked will drag them away, because they refuse to do justice.
pieces: The wicked are swept away by their own violence, \q since they will not do what is just.

L.7: [The] violence of [the] wicked will drag them away, \q because they refuse to do justice.

R.7: Wicked people will be destroyed by their own violence, \q because they will not do what is right.

decisions.choice: drag them away: their violence catches them like a net
decisions.reason: The verb (garar) is used of dragging fish in a net (Habakkuk 1:15). Violence turns back on those who use it (1:18–19).

records.source: הֲפַכְפַּ֬ךְ דֶּ֣רֶךְ אִ֣ישׁ וָזָ֑ר וְ֝זַ֗ךְ יָשָׁ֥ר פָּעֳלֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Very crooked [is the] way of a person guilty, and [the] pure, upright [is] his work.
pieces: The path of the guilty is twisted, \q but the conduct of the pure is straight.

L.8: [The] way of a guilty person [is] crooked, \q but [as for the] pure, {{gender:their|his}} conduct [is] upright.

R.8: Guilty people live crooked lives. \q But people who are pure in heart do what is right.

decisions.choice: crooked ... guilty: twisted ways of one laden with guilt
alternatives: the way of a person is crooked and strange
decisions.reason: Crooked (hafakpak) is a doubled form, "very twisted". The next word (wazar) appears only here; it is usually taken as "guilty" (from a word known in Arabic), but it can be divided as "and strange", giving "a person's way is twisted and strange".

records.source: ט֗וֹב לָשֶׁ֥בֶת עַל־פִּנַּת־גָּ֑ג מֵאֵ֥שֶׁת מִ֝דְיָנִ֗ים וּבֵ֥ית חָֽבֶר׃
records.gloss: Good to dwell on a corner of a roof more than a woman of contentions and a house of association.
pieces: It is better to live up in a corner of the rooftop \q than to share a home with a wife who quarrels.

L.9: [It is] better to live on a corner of [the] roof \q than [with] a woman of quarrels in a shared house.

R.9: It is better to live alone in a corner of a flat roof \q than to share a house with a wife who is always arguing.

decisions.choice: a corner of the roof: a cramped, exposed spot on a flat roof
decisions.reason: Houses had flat roofs used for work and sleep (Joshua 2:6; 1 Samuel 9:25). A corner up there is open to sun and rain, yet better than constant quarrels below. The saying is repeated in 25:24; compare verse 19 and 19:13.

decisions.choice: a house of association: a house shared with her
decisions.reason: The phrase (bet haver) means a house held in common. Some take it as a large or busy house, but sharing fits the contrast with living alone on the roof.

records.source: נֶ֣פֶשׁ רָ֭שָׁע אִוְּתָה־רָ֑ע לֹא־יֻחַ֖ן בְּעֵינָ֣יו רֵעֵֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: [The] appetite of a wicked [person] craves evil; his neighbor is not shown favor in his eyes.
pieces: The wicked hunger for evil; \q their neighbors find no mercy from them.

L.10: [The] soul of [the] wicked craves evil; \q {{gender:their|his}} neighbor finds no favor in {{gender:their|his}} eyes.

R.10: Wicked people want to do evil. \q They show no kindness to the people around them.

decisions.choice: soul craves: the appetite longs for
decisions.reason: The soul (nefesh) here is desire or appetite (13:4; 13:19). A wicked person's longing is for harm, so even a neighbor gets no pity.

records.source: בַּעְנָשׁ־לֵ֭ץיֶחְכַּם־פֶּ֑תִי וּבְהַשְׂכִּ֥יל לְ֝חָכָ֗ם יִקַּח־דָּֽעַת׃
records.gloss: When a mocker is fined, a naive person becomes wise; and when a wise [person] is instructed, he receives knowledge.
pieces: When a mocker is punished, the naive learn wisdom; \q when the wise are taught, they take in knowledge.

L.11: When a mocker is punished, [the] simple become wise; \q and when a wise [person] is instructed, {{gender:they gain|he gains}} knowledge.

R.11: When a mocker is punished, simple people watch and learn a lesson. \q Wise people learn just by being taught.

decisions.choice: the simple learn from the mocker's punishment, as in 19:25
decisions.reason: The mocker does not learn, but onlookers do (19:25). The wise need no punishment, only teaching (9:8–9).

decisions.choice: when a wise person is instructed
alternatives: when the simple one watches the wise, he gains knowledge
decisions.reason: The verb (haskil) can mean "to instruct" or "to pay attention"; the line may also continue with the simple person as subject, who learns by watching the wise. Either way, knowledge is gained.

decisions.choice: watch and learn a lesson
decisions.reason: Readable says how the simple learn, from seeing the punishment.

records.source: מַשְׂכִּ֣יל צַ֭דִּיק לְבֵ֣ית רָשָׁ֑ע מְסַלֵּ֖ף רְשָׁעִ֣ים לָרָֽע׃
records.gloss: [The] Righteous One gives attention to [the] house of [the] wicked; he subverts [the] wicked to calamity.
pieces: The Righteous One watches over the house of the wicked \q and throws the wicked down to ruin.

L.12: [The] Righteous One takes note of [the] house of [the] wicked; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} overthrows [the] wicked to ruin.

R.12: God, the Righteous One, sees what happens in the homes of the wicked. \q He brings wicked people to ruin.

decisions.choice: the Righteous One: God
alternatives: a righteous person observes the house of the wicked (and God overthrows them)
decisions.reason: The one who overthrows the wicked is most naturally God, who is called the Righteous One in Job 34:17 and Isaiah 24:16. Others take it as a righteous person who studies what happens to the wicked household, with God as the unnamed one who brings them down.

decisions.choice: God, the Righteous One
decisions.reason: Readable names God so the title is clear.

records.source: אֹטֵ֣ם אָ֭זְנוֹ מִזַּעֲקַת־דָּ֑ל גַּֽם־ה֥וּא יִ֝קְרָ֗א וְלֹ֣א יֵעָנֶֽה׃
records.gloss: [One who] shuts his ear from [the] cry of [the] poor, also he will call out and not be answered.
pieces: Whoever stops their ears to the cry of the poor \q will also call out one day and get no answer.

L.13: Whoever shuts {{gender:their|his}} ear to [the] cry of [the] poor, \q {{gender:they|he}} too will call out and not be answered.

R.13: If you will not listen when poor people cry for help, \q no one will answer when you cry for help.

decisions.choice: measure for measure: the deaf ear meets a deaf ear
decisions.reason: The unanswered call may be to people or to God (1:28; Psalm 18:42). The law commands care for the poor (Deuteronomy 15:7–11); compare 14:31; 19:17; Matthew 25:41–45.

decisions.choice: one day
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "one day" to show the turn comes later.

records.source: מַתָּ֣ן בַּ֭סֵּתֶר יִכְפֶּה־אָ֑ף וְשֹׁ֥חַד בַּ֝חֵ֗ק חֵמָ֥ה עַזָּֽה׃
records.gloss: A gift in secrecy subdues anger, and a bribe in [the] bosom, strong rage.
pieces: A gift given in secret calms anger, \q and a bribe tucked in the cloak quiets fierce rage.

L.14: A gift in secret subdues anger, \q and a bribe in [the] fold of [the] robe, fierce wrath.

R.14: A secret gift can calm someone's anger. \q A hidden bribe can cool down even great rage.

decisions.choice: a bribe in the bosom: slipped into the fold of a garment
decisions.reason: The fold of the robe served as a pocket (17:23). The saying observes how bribes work; it does not approve them (17:8, 23; 18:16; Exodus 23:8).

records.source: שִׂמְחָ֣ה לַ֭צַּדִּיק עֲשׂ֣וֹת מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּ֝מְחִתָּ֗ה לְפֹ֣עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃
records.gloss: [It is] a joy to the righteous [person] to do justice, and terror to [those who] do wickedness.
pieces: When justice is done, the righteous rejoice, \q but evildoers are filled with dread.

L.15: [It is a] joy to [the] righteous [when] justice [is] done, \q but terror to those who do wickedness.

R.15: Good people are glad when justice is done. \q But it frightens people who do evil.

decisions.choice: when justice is done
alternatives: for the righteous to do justice is a joy
decisions.reason: The infinitive "to do justice" names no doer. It may be the righteous who delight in doing right, or justice carried out by anyone, which cheers the righteous and terrifies the wicked. The contrast of joy and terror favors justice being carried out.

records.source: אָדָ֗ם תּ֭וֹעֶה מִדֶּ֣רֶךְ הַשְׂכֵּ֑ל בִּקְהַ֖ל רְפָאִ֣ים יָנֽוּחַ׃
records.gloss: A person [who] wanders from [the] way of insight will rest in [the] assembly of [the] shades.
pieces: Whoever strays from the path of good sense \q will come to rest in the company of the dead.

L.16: A person who wanders from [the] way of insight \q will rest in [the] assembly of [the] dead.

R.16: People who turn away from wisdom will end up among the dead.

decisions.choice: assembly of the dead: the shades (rephaim) in the grave
decisions.reason: The rephaim are the dead in Sheol (2:18; 9:18; Isaiah 14:9). "Rest" is pointed: the wanderer finally settles down, among the dead.

records.source: אִ֣ישׁ מַ֭חְסוֹר אֹהֵ֣ב שִׂמְחָ֑ה אֹהֵ֥ב יַֽיִן־וָ֝שֶׁ֗מֶן לֹ֣א יַעֲשִֽׁיר׃
records.gloss: A person of lack [will be one who] loves pleasure; [one who] loves wine and oil will not get rich.
pieces: Those who love pleasure will end up poor; \q those who love wine and fine oil will never be rich.

L.17: Whoever loves pleasure [will be] a person in want; \q whoever loves wine and oil will not grow rich.

R.17: People who live for fun will become poor. \q If you love fine wine and perfume, you will never be rich.

decisions.choice: wine and oil: the luxuries of feasting
decisions.reason: Oil for anointing the head went with wine at a feast (Psalm 23:5; 104:15; Amos 6:6). Living for such pleasures drains wealth (23:20–21).

decisions.choice: perfume
decisions.reason: Readable names the use of the oil, which was perfumed for the body, not for cooking.

records.source: כֹּ֣פֶר לַצַּדִּ֣יק רָשָׁ֑ע וְתַ֖חַת יְשָׁרִ֣ים בּוֹגֵֽד׃
records.gloss: A ransom for the righteous [is the] wicked, and in place of [the] upright, [one who] acts treacherously.
pieces: The wicked serve as ransom for the righteous, \q and the treacherous go in place of the upright.

L.18: [The] wicked [is] a ransom for [the] righteous, \q and in place of [the] upright, [comes the] treacherous.

R.18: The trouble that might have hit good people falls on the wicked instead. \q Those who betray others suffer in place of honest people.

decisions.choice: ransom: the wicked take the trouble the righteous escape
decisions.reason: As in 11:8, the righteous are rescued from trouble and the wicked fall into it in their place (compare Isaiah 43:3; Esther 7:10). It is not a payment for sin but a turn of fortune.

records.source: ט֗וֹב שֶׁ֥בֶת בְּאֶֽרֶץ־מִדְבָּ֑ר מֵאֵ֖שֶׁת מִדְיָנִ֣ים וָכָֽעַס׃
records.gloss: Good to dwell in a land of wilderness more than a woman of contentions and vexation.
pieces: It is better to live in the wilderness \q than with a wife who quarrels and frets.

L.19: [It is] better to live in a desert land \q than [with] a woman of quarrels and vexation.

R.19: It is better to live alone in the desert \q than with a wife who is always arguing and angry.

decisions.choice: quarrels (midyanim), as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) and the reading the scribes marked (qere) are two spellings of the same word. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: the desert: lonely and harsh, as in verse 9
decisions.reason: Verse 9 sends the man to a corner of the roof; here he goes further, to the wilderness. Vexation (kaas) is irritation or anger that she causes or shows.

records.source: אוֹצָ֤ר׀נֶחְמָ֣ד וָ֭שֶׁמֶן בִּנְוֵ֣ה חָכָ֑ם וּכְסִ֖יל אָדָ֣ם יְבַלְּעֶֽנּוּ׃
records.gloss: Treasure desirable and oil [are] in [the] habitation of a wise [person], and a fool of a person swallows it up.
pieces: Valuable treasure and oil are stored in the home of the wise, \q but a fool gulps it all down.

L.20: Precious treasure and oil [are] in [the] dwelling of [the] wise, \q but a foolish person swallows it up.

R.20: Wise people save good things in their homes. \q Foolish people use up everything they have.

decisions.choice: swallows it up: uses up at once
decisions.reason: The wise store up (10:14); the fool consumes whatever comes in and keeps nothing (verse 17).

records.source: רֹ֭דֵף צְדָקָ֣ה וָחָ֑סֶד יִמְצָ֥א חַ֝יִּ֗ים צְדָקָ֥ה וְכָבֽוֹד׃
records.gloss: [One who] pursues righteousness and loyalty finds life, righteousness, and honor.
pieces: Whoever chases after what is right and loyal love \q finds life, vindication, and honor.

L.21: Whoever pursues righteousness and loyal love \q finds life, righteousness, and honor.

R.21: If you work hard to do what is right and to show faithful love, \q you will find life. \q You will be treated rightly, and people will honor you.

decisions.choice: righteousness found: being set right, vindicated
decisions.reason: The same word (tsedaqah) is pursued and then found. What is found is the reward of right living: being in the right and treated as such (8:18; Isaiah 54:17).

decisions.choice: loyal love (hesed)
decisions.reason: Faithful kindness, as in 3:3 and 20:28.

records.source: עִ֣יר גִּ֭בֹּרִים עָלָ֣ה חָכָ֑ם וַ֝יֹּ֗רֶד עֹ֣ז מִבְטֶחָֽה׃
records.gloss: A city of warriors a wise [person] goes up and brought down [the] strength of its confidence.
pieces: A wise person can scale a city held by warriors \q and pull down the stronghold they relied on.

L.22: A wise [person] goes up [against the] city of [the] mighty \q and brings down [the] stronghold of its confidence.

R.22: One wise person can capture a city full of strong soldiers. \q Wisdom can bring down the walls they trusted in.

decisions.choice: wisdom is stronger than might
decisions.reason: Compare 24:5–6 and Ecclesiastes 9:13–16: wisdom wins where strength fails. The stronghold of its confidence is the wall the city trusts.

records.source: שֹׁמֵ֣ר פִּ֭יו וּלְשׁוֹנ֑וֹ שֹׁמֵ֖ר מִצָּר֣וֹת נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃
records.gloss: [One who] guards his mouth and his tongue [is] keeping from troubles his self.
pieces: Whoever watches their mouth and tongue \q keeps themselves out of trouble.

L.23: Whoever guards {{gender:their|his}} mouth and {{gender:their|his}} tongue \q keeps {{gender:themselves|himself}} from troubles.

R.23: If you are careful about what you say, \q you will stay out of trouble.

decisions.choice: guards ... keeps: the same verb twice
decisions.reason: The verb (shamar) is used for both halves: guard your speech and you guard your life (13:3; 18:21).

records.source: זֵ֣ד יָ֭הִיר לֵ֣ץ שְׁמ֑וֹ ע֝וֹשֶׂ֗ה בְּעֶבְרַ֥ת זָדֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: An arrogant [person], proud, mocker [is] his name, acting in [an] overflowing of presumption.
pieces: The proud and haughty earn the name of mocker; \q they act with boundless arrogance.

L.24: [The] arrogant [and] haughty, mocker [is] {{gender:their|his}} name; \q {{gender:they act|he acts}} in [an] overflow of pride.

R.24: Proud and arrogant people are called mockers. \q They act as if they were better than everyone.

decisions.choice: a definition of the mocker
decisions.reason: The saying names what a mocker (lets) is: one full of pride whose arrogance overflows (1:22; 9:7–8; 22:10). Pride (zadon) is presumption that sets itself above others and God (13:10).

records.source: תַּאֲוַ֣ת עָצֵ֣ל תְּמִיתֶ֑נּוּ כִּֽי־מֵאֲנ֖וּ יָדָ֣יו לַעֲשֽׂוֹת׃
records.gloss: [The] desire of a sluggard kills him, because his hands refuse to work.
pieces: The lazy one's cravings will be the death of them, \q because their hands refuse to work.

L.25: [The] craving of [the] sluggard kills {{gender:them|him}}, \q for {{gender:their|his}} hands refuse to work.

R.25: Lazy people want many things, but they will not work for them. \q In the end, their wishes kill them.

decisions.choice: desire that kills: longing without labor
decisions.reason: The lazy one wants but will not work (13:4; 19:24); unmet need leads to ruin and even death.

records.source: כָּל־הַ֭יּוֹם הִתְאַוָּ֣ה תַאֲוָ֑ה וְצַדִּ֥יק יִ֝תֵּ֗ן וְלֹ֣א יַחְשֹֽׂךְ׃
records.gloss: All the day he craves a craving, and a righteous [person] gives and does not hold back.
pieces: All day long the lazy only crave more, \q but the righteous give without holding back.

L.26: All day long {{gender:they crave|he craves}} [more], \q but [the] righteous [person] gives and does not hold back.

R.26: Lazy people want more and more all day long. \q But good people give freely and do not hold anything back.

decisions.choice: he craves: the sluggard of verse 25
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject; it continues the sluggard of verse 25, whose endless wanting is set against the generosity of the righteous.

decisions.choice: the lazy
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject carried over from verse 25.

records.source: זֶ֣בַח רְ֭שָׁעִים תּוֹעֵבָ֑ה אַ֝֗ף כִּֽי־בְזִמָּ֥ה יְבִיאֶֽנּוּ׃
records.gloss: [The] sacrifice of [the] wicked [is] an abomination; how much more when with evil intent he brings it.
pieces: The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable, \q and all the more when it is offered with evil intent.

L.27: [The] sacrifice of [the] wicked [is] an abomination; \q how much more when {{gender:they bring|he brings}} it with evil intent!

R.27: The offerings of wicked people are disgusting. \q They are even worse when given as part of an evil plan.

decisions.choice: the sacrifice of the wicked, as in 15:8
decisions.reason: 15:8 says the same, adding "to the LORD". Here the further step is a sacrifice brought with evil intent (zimmah, a scheme), perhaps to win God's help for a crime or to buy him off (verse 3).

records.source: עֵד־כְּזָבִ֥ים יֹאבֵ֑ד וְאִ֥ישׁ שׁ֝וֹמֵ֗עַ לָנֶ֥צַח יְדַבֵּֽר׃
records.gloss: A witness of lies will perish, and a person [who] listens to perpetuity will speak.
pieces: A false witness will perish, \q but one who listens carefully will speak with lasting effect.

L.28: A lying witness will perish, \q but a person who listens will speak to [the] end.

R.28: A witness who lies will be destroyed. \q But people who listen carefully will be heard, and their words will last.

decisions.choice: speak to the end: testimony that stands
decisions.reason: The phrase (lanetsah) is "for ever" or "to the end". The one who listens, who reports only what was truly heard, gives testimony that lasts and is not overturned, unlike the false witness (19:5, 9). It may also mean such a person will always be allowed to speak.

records.source: הֵעֵ֬ז אִ֣ישׁ רָשָׁ֣ע בְּפָנָ֑יו וְ֝יָשָׁ֗ר ה֤וּא׀יָבִ֬ין דַּרְכּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: A wicked person makes his face firm, and an upright [person], he considers his way.
pieces: The wicked put on a bold face, \q but the upright give thought to the way they go.

L.29: A wicked person puts on a bold face, \q but [the] upright, {{gender:they consider|he considers}} {{gender:their|his}} way.

R.29: Wicked people act tough and shameless. \q But good people think carefully about how they live.

decisions.choice: makes his face firm: puts on a hard, shameless face
decisions.reason: As in 7:13, a hard face is brazen confidence that brushes aside conscience.

decisions.choice: considers, as the scribes' reading has it
alternatives: makes his way sure (the written form)
decisions.reason: The reading the scribes marked (qere) is "considers" (yavin); the written consonants (ketiv) read "establishes" (yakhin), "makes his way firm", answering the wicked one's firm face. Both set the upright one's steady path against the wicked one's bluster.

records.source: אֵ֣ין חָ֭כְמָה וְאֵ֣ין תְּבוּנָ֑ה וְאֵ֥ין עֵ֝צָ֗ה לְנֶ֣גֶד יְהוָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: There [is] no wisdom and there [is] no understanding and there [is] no counsel against YHWH.
pieces: No wisdom, no understanding, \q no plan can stand against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.30: There [is] no wisdom and no understanding \q and no counsel against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.30: No amount of wisdom, understanding, or planning can succeed against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: against the LORD
alternatives: before the LORD (in comparison with him)
decisions.reason: The phrase (leneged) is "in front of, opposite". Human wisdom cannot oppose the LORD, nor does it compare with his (19:21; Isaiah 8:10; Job 5:12–13).

records.source: ס֗וּס מ֭וּכָן לְי֣וֹם מִלְחָמָ֑ה וְ֝לַֽיהוָ֗ה הַתְּשׁוּעָֽה׃
records.gloss: A horse [is] prepared for a day of battle, and to YHWH [belongs] the victory.
pieces: People ready the horse for the day of battle, \q yet the victory belongs to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.31: A horse [is] made ready for [the] day of battle, \q but to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [belongs] the victory.

R.31: People get their horses ready for war. \q But only {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} can give them the victory.

decisions.choice: the horse: the war horse and chariot
decisions.reason: Horses were used mainly in war, drawing chariots; they stood for military power (Deuteronomy 17:16; Psalm 20:8; 33:17).

decisions.choice: victory (teshuah): deliverance, rescue
decisions.reason: The word is rescue or victory in battle (1 Samuel 11:13; Psalm 33:17). Preparation is right, but the outcome is the LORD's (16:1, 9; 19:21). A new paragraph begins here in the manuscript tradition.
